questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I stayed ______ my uncle's house last night.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I stayed ______ my uncle's house last night.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'at.'

Key Points

  • Let us look at the usage of the given options:
    • At: used when you are at the top, bottom or end of something; at a specific address; at a general location; and at a point. (At” का उपयोग तब किया जाता है जब आप किसी चीज़ के ऊपर, नीचे या अंत में होते हैं; एक विशिष्ट पते पर; एक सामान्य स्थान पर; और एक बिंदु पर।)
    • On: used for something resting upon or atop something else. (किसी चीज़ के ऊपर या किसी चीज़ के ऊपर आराम करने के लिए इस्तेमाल किया जाता है।)
    • In: used for something inside or enclosed by something else. (किसी चीज के अंदर या किसी चीज से घिरे होने के लिए इस्तेमाल किया जाता है।)
    • By: When we use the passive voice, we can use a phrase with by to say who did the action. (जब हम Passive voice का उपयोग करते हैं, तो हम यह कहने के लिए  by का उपयोग कर सकते हैं कि किसने कार्रवाई की।)
  • Correct sentence: I stayed at my uncle's house last night. 

Additional Information
   

  • We can use not … ever instead of never, but never is much more common.
    • Example: She has never been a friend of ours.

questions.question: In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. I write ______ my sister every month.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.

I write ______ my sister every month.
questions.solution:
Correct option - 3

Here, concept of preposition is brought under consideration.

Let's find out the uses of all the given options :-

In - Used to describe the position of someone or something in an enclosed area or place surrounding it.

Of - Used for belonging to, relating to, or connected with someone or something; to indicate reference.

To - Used when there is a specific destination in mind.

At - Used for precise times.

With reference to the context, letter is written to her sister. Hence, preposition to should be used here. Thus, option 3 i.e. to is the correct answer.

Correct sentence - I write to my sister every month.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The early computers were ______ for basic tasks only.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The early computers were ______ for basic tasks only.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'designed'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is talking about the specific purpose behind the creation of the early computers.
  • 'Designed' means planned or created in detail or for a specific purpose.
    • Example: Jeeps are rugged vehicles, designed for rough conditions.
  • Therefore, the most appropriate word to be filled in the blank is the verb 'designed'.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Complete Sentence: The early computers were designed for basic tasks only.

Additional Information

  • Let us explore the other options:
    • Performed means carried out, accomplished, or fulfilled an action, task, or function.
    • Arranged means organized or made plans for a future event.
    • Achieved means successfully reached a desired objective or result by effort, skill, or courage.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with an appropriate option. He could feel every ______ and artery in his body.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The Covid-19 pandemic has hit many industries really _______.

The Covid-19 pandemic has hit many industries really _______.
questions.solution:

Key Points

    •  Example: The speaker tried hard to impress the audience.
  •  The adverb 'hard' should be used in the context of the sentence.

Additional Information

  • Hardly- scarcely (used to qualify a statement by saying that it is true to an insignificant degree).

questions.question: Direction: A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative. I smiled at my son and ______ thankful.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

I smiled at my son and ______ thankful.
questions.solution: The reason "felt" is the correct option is because it aligns with the past tense structure of the sentence. The sentence is describing an action that already happened—smiling at the son—and the feeling of thankfulness that occurred at that moment. Therefore, the past tense form "felt" is the appropriate choice. The other options (fallen, feel, feeling) either don't match the tense or are not suitable in the context of the sentence. Correct sentence: I smiled at my son and felt thankful.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. She left _____ Mumbai ______ the Rajdhani Express yesterday.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

She left _____ Mumbai ______ the Rajdhani Express yesterday.
questions.solution:
Let's understand the options and find the correct answer.

prepositions showing time and  position  include: at, on, in

preposition showing movement  is: to

prepositions showing purpose  is for:

prepositions used in a passive sentence is: by

Option 1 (to; at) is incorrect as both the prepositions are wrong for the given blanks.

Option 2 ( for; by) is correct as it correctly expresses the meaning.

Option 3 (out; by) is incorrect as the first part is incorrect for the sentence.

Option 4 (in; in) is incorrect as both the prepositions are incorrect.

Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Directions: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate words. Rohit taught you such tricks as these, ________?

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I wish we had ______ come here.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I wish we had ______ come here.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3)

Key Points

  • The sentence expresses a wish about a past action, indicating regret or a desire that something had not happened.
  • The word "never" is appropriate in this context as it correctly conveys the speaker's regret about coming to the place.
  • Other options like "right," "clear," and "agreed" do not fit the context of the sentence and do not convey the intended meaning of regret or wish.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: I wish we had never come here.

Additional Information

  • The word "never" is often used in sentences that express a wish or regret about something that did not happen in the past.
  • It is important to choose words that correctly convey the intended meaning and fit the grammatical structure of the sentence.

questions.question: Direction: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option. I have been on this project since the first day, hence I am responsible ______ it.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence. The vase broke _________ pieces when Simran dropped it.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.

The vase broke _________ pieces when Simran dropped it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

'In' is used when something is enclosed within the other.

'Into' is used to describe the movement to show division.

'Among' is used when something is divided between three or more people.

'From' is used to denote the initial point of something.

In the given sentence, the vase broke and was divided into a number of pieces. So, the most appropriate word is 'into'.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank. The team __________ the championship before their star player got injured.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank.
The team __________ the championship before their star player got injured.
questions.solution:
```html

The correct answer is 'had won' i.e. this part of the sentence is correct.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the use of the past perfect tense 'had won' is correct as it indicates an action that was completed before another action in the past (the star player got injured).
  • The past perfect tense is used to show that an action was completed before another action in the past.
  • Therefore, the past perfect form of the verb 'had won' is used correctly in this context.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: The team had won the championship before their star player got injured.

Additional Information

  • The past perfect tense is often used in sentences to show a sequence of past events, where one event occurred before the other.
    • Example: By the time we arrived at the station, the train had left.
  • It is important to use the correct tense to convey the intended meaning and timeline of events accurately.
    • Example: She had finished her homework before she went out to play.
```

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. You must apologize ______ the punishment.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank in the given sentence. We must not take the future for granted; rather, we should enjoy the ______ joys of our humdrum lives.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Rohan is quite popular ______ his classmates.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence. I was walking along the street when suddenly I ______ footsteps behind me.

  • So, the correct word is heard.

questions.question: The sentence(s) given with blanks are to be filled with an appropriate word(s). Four alternatives are suggested for each question. For each question, choose the correct alternative and click the button corresponding to it. Risha ______ a salary of Rs 50,000 every month.

So the sentence is in the simple present tense and must have the following format : Sub + V1 + s/es + object. Since Risha is a singular subject, the singular verb ‘earns’ should be used.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My teacher is the ______ of all.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

My teacher is the ______ of all.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'kindest'

Key Points

The sentence refers to one teacher and her attribute among the others. Her kindness is the highest among all the teachers.

A superlative degree is used to choose one out of a group or many.

  • Base form: kind
  • Comparative: kinder
  • Superlative: kindest

Thus kindest is the most suitable option.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Keeping distance from others is one of the ______ one must take to remain safe from the coronavirus.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

Keeping distance from others is one of the ______ one must take to remain safe from the coronavirus.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Precautions.

Key Points

  •  The most appropriate word to fill in the blank is precautions. 
  •  Here in this sentence, we have to take certain safety measures to protect ourselves from coronavirus by keeping a distance from others.
  •  As 'safety measures' and 'precautions' are synonyms for each other.
  •  Precautions mean a measure taken in advance to prevent something dangerous, unpleasant, or inconvenient from happening.
    • ​Example: Ensure to fasten your seatbelt, which is a precautionary measure for safe driving of the car.
  •  By looking at the meaning from above, we can say that the correct answer to this question is option 4. i.e. precautions.

 

Correct Sentence: Keeping distance from others is one of the precautions one must take to remain safe from the coronavirus.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The boy was leaning against the pillar ______ his hands ______ his pockets.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.
The boy was leaning against the pillar ______ his hands ______ his pockets.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, 'With; in'.

  • The sentence carries the concept of Preposition. 
  • 'With' is applicable for 'connection of two objects'. The boy and the pillar are in contact with each other. Hence, 'With' is the correct preposition used. 
  • 'In' is applicable for 'inside'. The hands of the boy went 'inside' his pockets. Hence, 'in' is the correct preposition used. 

Thus and so, option 3 is the correct option.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Yesterday, Mohini ______ her brother to lend her a pen.

questions.solution:

  • The given sentence refers to an incident which has happened yesterday.
  • Hence we require a past tense verb to fill the blank. Also, the subject is singular and we need a singular verb here.
  • Let us look at the options given:

  • request’ is a plural verb and is inappropriate for the given blank.
  • ‘has requested’ is present perfect tense, hence inappropriate for the given blank.
  • ‘requested’ is a singular past tense verb and aptly fits in the given blank. Hence the correct option is Option 4 i.e. ‘requested’.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to ﬁll in the blank and make a meaningful sentence. Which _______ should we adopt to increase our sales?

Functions means practical use or purpose in design.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Ours is ________ house of all the houses in our area.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Ours is ________ house of all the houses in our area.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: the biggest.

Key Points

  • The sentence requires the use of a superlative form because it is comparing one house with all others in the area.
  • "The biggest" is the correct superlative form of "big."
  • The phrases "the more bigger" and "the most biggest" are grammatically incorrect because "bigger" and "biggest" already convey comparative and superlative degrees respectively.
  • "The bigger" is a comparative form and is not suitable for a comparison among more than two entities.

Therefore, the correct sentence is: Ours is the biggest house of all the houses in our area.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She treats her juniors _____ contempt.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She treats her juniors _____ contempt.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'with'.

  • Options 1, 3, and 4 are incorrect because they do not form a proper collocation with the word "contempt."

  • Option 3: "in contempt" is incorrect because it changes the meaning of the sentence and does not indicate the act of treating someone with disdain.
  • Option 4: "for contempt" is incorrect because it does not fit the grammatical structure of the sentence.

questions.question: In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. He has been ______ here since 1997.

The correct answer is 'is'

Key Points

  • According to the rule of grammar, whenever the subject of the sentence is singular then we need to use a singular verb for the singular noun.
  • In the given sentence, the subject of the sentence 'park' there is an adverb hence, we need to use a singular verb so the correct answer is 'is'
  • Let's see an example-
    • There's someone on the phone for you.
  • In the given sentence, 'there' is an adverb which means that 'there is used to introduce the subject of a sentence, especially before the verbs be, seem, and appear'

So the correct sentence is- There is a big park in front of our house.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Do not meddle ______ the affairs of others.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

Do not meddle ______ the affairs of others.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

Out of given alternatives, the correct preposition that fits in the given context is 'in', which is used to mean 'involved in something; taking part in something'.

In the given sentence, 'do not meddle in' means not to involve in the affairs of others.

The correct sentence is 'Do not meddle in the affairs of others.'

questions.question: In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. Four braces of partridges ______ been bought.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.

Four braces of partridges ______ been bought.
questions.solution:
Correct option - 1

Here, concept of passive voice is brought under consideration. Sometimes, subject is not mentioned in the passive voice, thus use of by is also omitted. Since, blank is followed by been which is used with forms of 'have'. That is, 

Object + has/have + been + Verb's 3rd form.

So, options 3 & 4 are eliminated. Since, object is four braces which is a plural noun. Hence, plural verb to be used. So, option 2 is eliminated. Thus, option 1 i.e. have is the correct answer. 

Correct sentence - Four braces of partridges have been bought.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. ______ I learned that there was a gift for each child, I was delighted.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

______ I learned that there was a gift for each child, I was delighted.
questions.solution: The correct answer is "When". "When" is a conjunction that indicates a point in time, and it is commonly used to introduce a clause that specifies the time something happened. In this sentence, "when" is the most appropriate option to fill in the blank because it introduces the clause that explains the specific time the speaker became delighted, which is when they learned that there was a gift for each child.

questions.question: Direction: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option. Though poor, he ______ proud of his learning.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Though poor, he ______ proud of his learning.
questions.solution: In this context, "was" is the correct past tense form of the verb "to be" to maintain grammatical consistency with the subject "he." In this sentence, "he" is the subject, and the verb needs to agree with it in terms of tense. Since the sentence is describing a past state of being, the past tense form of the verb "to be" is required, which is "was" for the singular subject "he." Additionally, "was" maintains the parallel structure with the adjective "proud" to convey that despite his poverty, he possessed pride in his learning. Therefore, "was" is the most suitable option to complete the sentence grammatically and semantically. Correct sentence: Though poor, he was proud of his learning.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. You will find it difficult ______ but later you will get used to wearing a mask.

questions.solution: The most appropriate option for the given blank is 'at first'. The phrase ‘at first’ means at the 'at the beginning. Example: At first, I thought he was joking, but then I realized he was serious.

questions.question: A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative. I am not sure _______ wearing this black dress.
questions.questionHtml:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative. 

I am not sure _______ wearing this black dress.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 3' i.e. 'About'.
Key Points
  • We have to identify the most appropriate preposition that will express the speaker's uncertainty about wearing the black dress.
  • The preposition "about" is used after being "sure" or "unsure" to introduce the thing that is being considered or questioned.
  • Therefore, the correct preposition to complete the sentence is "about": "I am not sure about wearing this black dress."
  • This implies the speaker is uncertain or has doubts about whether to wear the mentioned black dress.
Therefore, the correct answer is: 'About'.
Additional Information
  • "With" (Option 1): "With" is a preposition used to express being accompanied by or having something. In this context, it does not accurately convey the speaker's uncertainty about wearing the dress.
  • "In" (Option 2): "In" is used to indicate location or state, not uncertainty or doubt. It's not the correct choice in this sentence.
  • "Off" (Option 4): "Off" is normally used as a preposition to indicate removal or separation or to indicate a location that is not central. It does not fit into this sentence to convey the intended meaning of ambiguity or doubt.

questions.question: In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word.Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. They refuse ______ work for their living.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word.Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.

They refuse ______ work for their living.
questions.solution:
Correct option - 1

Here, concept of to + infinitive verb is brought under consideration. Infinitive verbs are not adjusted according to the subject. It means main verb is used as it is. Hence, its correct form is to+V1. So, option 1 i.e. to is the correct answer.

Note :- Preposition for is used with verb+ing.

Correct sentence - They refuse to work for their living.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Nobody in the village was prepared ______ the tragic news.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Nobody in the village was prepared ______ the tragic news.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "for"

Key Points

  •  Let's see the meaning of given words in the options.
    • TO (Preposition) is used in the direction of; as far as
      • Example:- He is going to Delhi.
    • With (Preposition) in the company of somebody/something.
      • Example:- I am working with my friends.
    • For ((Preposition) used as a function word to indicate purpose.
      • Example:-  I am waiting for my train.
    • of (Preposition) belonging to, connected with, or part of something/somebody
      • Example:- belonging to, connected with, or part of something/somebody
    • The village was prepared for the news (Intention for the thing.)
  • Hence, the correct answer is "FOR" The correct Sentence will be "Nobody in the village was prepared for the tragic news.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The group of travellers were wonderstruck by the ________ of the coin.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The group of travellers were wonderstruck by the ________ of the coin.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: weight.

Key Points

  • The blank in the sentence "The group of travellers were wonder struck by the ______ of the coin." calls for a noun that can be a characteristic of the coin that would amaze the travellers.
  • "Weight" fits this context as it is a physical attribute that can be surprising, especially if the coin is unexpectedly heavy or light. (वजन)
    • For example: The weight of the backpack made it difficult to walk long distances.
  • The options "wait," "white," and "wide" do not logically fit the context of something surprising about a coin's attribute.

Therefore, the correct answer is: weight.

Additional Information

  • "Wait" refers to a period of time for delaying until a certain event or time, which does not logically fit in the context of the coin's properties. (प्रतीक्षा)
    • For example: They had a long wait at the doctor's office.
  • "White" is a color, and it would be unusual to describe a coin using this term since coins are not typically noted for their color when causing wonder. (सफेद)
    • ​For example: The bride wore a beautiful white dress on her wedding day.
  • "Wide" refers to something having a certain breadth or width, which could be noteworthy for a coin, but it is less likely to cause amazement compared to the weight of a coin. (चौड़ा)
    • ​For example: The river was too wide to cross without a bridge.
